categories.main_business_segments: Lazard operates two primary business segments: Financial Advisory and Asset Management. The Financial Advisory segment offers corporate, partnership, institutional, government, sovereign and individual clients a wide array of financial advisory services including strategic and mergers and acquisitions advisory, capital markets advisory, shareholder advisory, restructuring and capital solutions, sovereign advisory, geopolitical advisory, capital raising and placement, and other strategic advisory matters. The Asset Management segment offers a broad range of global investment solutions and investment and wealth management services in equity and fixed income strategies, asset allocation strategies, alternative investments and private equity funds to corporations, public funds, sovereign entities, endowments and foundations, labor funds, financial intermediaries and private clients.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Lazard's core methodologies include fundamental security selection and analysis for asset management, incorporating quantitative analysis, accounting analysis, security selection and portfolio construction, risk management, and ESG factors. The Financial Advisory business relies on senior-level professional expertise in transaction analysis and execution, valuation analyses, fairness opinions, and strategic advisory. The Asset Management business employs proprietary systems including quantitative models designed and maintained by investment teams, along with global research capabilities and in-house investment analysts across all products and platforms.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Financial Advisory serves corporations, governments, institutions, partnerships and individuals globally, with particular focus on cross-border transactions and large capitalization M&A. Asset Management serves corporations, public funds, sovereign entities, endowments and foundations, labor funds, financial intermediaries and private clients, with approximately 85% of AUM managed for institutional clients and 15% for individual client relationships including family offices and high-net-worth individuals. The company serves clients across major industry groups including consumer, financial institutions, health care and life sciences, industrials, power and energy/infrastructure, real estate, technology, and telecommunications, media and entertainment.
categories.geographic_coverage: Lazard operates from 43 cities across 26 countries in North and South America, Europe, Asia and Australia. The company maintains major local presence in the United States, the United Kingdom and France, with regional branch offices in the U.S. and presence in Argentina, Belgium, Brazil, Canada, Chile, China, Colombia, Germany, Hong Kong, Italy, Japan, Mexico, the Netherlands, Panama, Singapore, Spain, Sweden and the Middle East region. Principal offices are located in New York City, Paris and London.
categories.supply_chain_position: Lazard operates as a downstream financial services provider, positioned at the advisory and asset management end of the financial services value chain. The company provides advisory services to clients undertaking transactions and manages assets on behalf of institutional and individual investors. Lazard does not manufacture products but rather provides intellectual capital and advisory services, relying on third-party service providers for execution and settlement of securities transactions.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include investing in intellectual capital through senior professionals with strong client relationships and industry expertise, increasing contacts with existing clients to enhance long-term relationships, developing new client relationships, expanding breadth and depth of industry expertise, coordinating industry specialty activities globally, selectively bolstering presence in local markets, broadening geographic presence, investing in technology infrastructure and data science capabilities, and deploying intellectual capital to generate new revenue streams. In Asset Management, the focus is on delivering superior investment performance and client service, broadening product offerings and distribution, enhancing investment performance, strengthening marketing and consultant relations capabilities, expanding product platforms, and continuing geographic expansion.
categories.revenue_model: Lazard generates revenue primarily through advisory fees from Financial Advisory services, which are typically payable upon successful completion of transactions or restructurings, and through investment management fees from Asset Management services based on assets under management. Asset Management fees are predominantly based on daily, monthly or quarterly average AUM, with additional performance-based incentive fees earned on various investment products. The company also earns retainer fees for certain engagements, fees from strategic advice not dependent on specific transactions, and fees from public and private securities offerings.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Lazard competes with other investment banking and financial advisory firms, broker-dealers, commercial and universal banks, insurance companies, investment management firms, hedge fund management firms, alternative investment firms, private banks and other financial institutions. The company positions itself as an independent advisor with a global footprint and unique competitive advantages including its independent advisory perspective, absence of conflicts from proprietary trading or lending operations, and deep roots in business centers worldwide. Many competitors are large consolidated financial institutions with broader product offerings, while boutique firms compete on independent advice basis.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: Lazard is a large accelerated filer with consolidated net revenue of $2.77 billion for the year ended December 31, 2022, compared to $3.19 billion in 2021, representing a 13% decrease. Net income attributable to Lazard Ltd was $358 million in 2022 compared to $528 million in 2021. The company had approximately 3,402 full-time employees as of December 31, 2022 across 43 cities in 26 countries. Asset Management AUM totaled $216 billion at December 31, 2022, down from $274 billion at December 31, 2021, primarily due to market depreciation and net outflows.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Lazard differentiates itself through its independent advisory perspective without conflicts from proprietary trading or lending operations, global footprint with local expertise in major business centers, senior-level attention from managing directors who actively participate in client engagements, teams of professionals indigenous to respective regions with long-term client relationships and regional expertise, coordination of global sector expertise with local knowledge, intellectual capital and strong client relationships developed since 1848, and ability to provide sophisticated customized solutions. The company emphasizes solving clients' most complex issues and providing advice to key decision-makers and senior management.
